title: Benchmark It Yourself (BIY): Preparing a Dataset and Benchmarking AI Models for Scatterplot-Related Tasks

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.2 ('o3-2025-04-16 (o3) and o4-mini-2025-04-16 (o4-mini) with the temperature set to 1 and reasoning effort to medium'). o3 is a reasoning model, so the runner drops temperature and sends max_completion_tokens plus reasoning_effort; max_tokens is ours.

task.subset_rule: the benchmark sample of Sec. 3.2: 115 data samples (25 Gaussian blobs, 25 Gaussian blobs with background noise, 50 Gaussian blobs with outliers, 7 random patterns, 8 relationships) x 15 chart designs = 1,725 scatterplots, task = cluster counting, prompting strategy = few-shot
task.approximation: Blocked before an approximation can be chosen - see open_points.

items.source: https://github.com/feedzai/biy-paper (Apache-2.0): dataset/input/images (18,921 PNGs), dataset/input/metadata (18,921 JSONs with cluster counts, bounding boxes and outlier coordinates), dataset/input/datasets (371 data samples), plus the Vega-Lite + Playwright generation pipeline and the benchmark scripts
items.config_or_split: the 1,725-image benchmark sample drawn by dataset/sample_dataset.py from the 18,921-image dataset

fields.input: the scatterplot PNG (image input, detail level 'high' for all OpenAI models)
fields.label: cluster_count from the matching metadata JSON

items.access_note: GET on 2026-09-19: the repository is reachable and dataset/input/images and dataset/input/metadata each list 18,921 files. Nothing downloaded - see the open point on the 50 MB limit.

prompt.user_template: How many clusters are there in the scatterplot? Answer with a number in curly brackets, e.g., {4}.

placeholders.image: the scatterplot PNG, sent as an image content part alongside this text - NOT expressible in the runner's text-only mini-language

prompt.few_shot: k = 6 worked examples in turn-based conversation format, 'randomly selected from the complete dataset, before it was sampled, to represent each of the benchmarked data generators (plus an extra one so that the few-shot prompts would include two examples with outliers)' (Sec. 3.2). WHICH six is not stated in the paper.
prompt.source_location: Sec. 3.2, the first of the five verbatim zero-shot task prompts
prompt.verbatim: full for the zero-shot instruction (extraction repairs only: the curly-bracket example survived intact, the surrounding bullet formatting dropped). Note a discrepancy worth recording: the repository's benchmark/prompts.py carries the same sentence with '{9}' as the example rather than the paper's '{4}'. The few-shot wrapper - how the six examples are laid out as prior turns - is described but not printed.

output.postprocess: Sec. 3.3: 'The raw responses were processed to extract the counts ... according to the prompts'; between 70.2% and 99.95% of OpenAI responses were counted as valid per model, so a validity rule is part of the protocol and is not spelled out

metric.name: mean_abs_error
metric.definition: MAE between the predicted and annotated cluster count over the 1,725 benchmark scatterplots.
metric.original_location: Sec. 3.3.1: 'the best value for cluster counting is 0.03 (o3 when few-shot prompted), while the worst is 1.46 (Flash-Lite (Thinking) when one-shot prompted)'

cost.prepare_note: not prepared. Rough order: 1,725 calls each carrying 7 high-detail images (6 few-shot examples plus the query) at o3's $2/$8 per 1M, plus hidden reasoning tokens. The paper's own total was ~$666 for 258,750 requests across 10 models and all 5 tasks x 3 strategies, i.e. well under a cent per request via the Batch API.

open_points: Image input. Every item is a scatterplot PNG; the runner's mini-language builds text-only messages, so a hook's render() would have to emit image content parts with base64 data URIs (as the Tier A TURTLEAI adapter does) and the request and call archives would then carry inline images. That is a real but non-trivial build, and it needs a decision because it changes what the archives contain.

The 50 MB download limit. The 1,725 benchmark images are individual files in dataset/input/images (18,921 in total); fetching only the sample still means ~1,725 separate raw.githubusercontent requests and, at typical optimized-PNG sizes, plausibly more than 50 MB. Regenerating them instead means running the repo's Vega-Lite + Playwright + Oxipng pipeline locally.

The sample is not identified in the paper. Sec. 3.2 names the composition (115 data samples x 15 chart designs) but not which 115; the draw lives in dataset/sample_dataset.py. Likewise the six few-shot examples are 'randomly selected' with no ids given, and the few-shot turn layout is described rather than printed - so the exact prompt for the claim cell cannot be reconstructed from the paper.
Prompt text discrepancy between the paper and the released code (paper '{4}', repository prompts.py '{9}'). Minor, but it has to be resolved before the comparison is called like-for-like.
notes: Everything about this paper is pinned except the parts that matter for a text-only batch runner: all 10 snapshots are named exactly, temperature and reasoning effort are stated, the five zero-shot prompts are printed verbatim, the dataset and the whole pipeline are public under Apache-2.0, and the run window (29 July - 5 August 2025) and total cost are reported. The claim cell is also a near-ceiling value (MAE 0.03 means o3 miscounts about 1 scatterplot in 30), so it is one-sided: it can only get worse. If the image-input hook is built once it would unlock several other cells of this paper and probably other multimodal Tier B papers too, which is the argument for treating this as an infrastructure decision rather than a per-paper one.
